speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision and floaters in the right eye, I need to ask a few questions and order some tests.

How long have you noticed these visual changes, and do the black spots move or stay fixed in one spot?

REQUEST TEST: Ocular_Coagulation_Serology (CMV, Toxoplasma)
REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy_Right_Eye

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CD4_T-lymphocyte: 36/mm3; Fundoscopy_Right_Eye: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages; Ocular_Coagulation_Serology: Data not available in current record.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: AIDS, fungal esophagitis treated with fluconazole, Kaposi's sarcoma Social history: No additional information provided

speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an interesting report from your previous doctor, but in an AIDS patient, decreased vision and floaters are most commonly caused by CMV retinitis, Toxoplasmosis, or Cytomegalovirus retinitis rather than Tuberculosis. Since I have already ordered a Coagulation Serology for CMV and Toxoplasma, I need to see the actual results of your fundoscopy and ask if you have had any flu-like symptoms or fever recently.

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy_Right_Eye
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
How have you been feeling generally, and have you experienced any fevers or fatigue lately?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy_Right_Eye: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages; CD4_T-lymphocyte: 36/mm3; Complete_Blood_Count: Data not available in current record.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis

The fundoscopy results showing granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in a patient with a CD4 count of 36/mm3 are classic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis. I do not need to pursue the tuberculosis theory mentioned earlier given these specific findings.
